summary: A DEV Community tutorial by Alexander Opalic on persisting user settings such as a dark mode preference with LocalStorage in Vue. It shows a basic component that saves and loads a darkMode value via localStorage.setItem and JSON parsing, then lists problems with that approach (type safety, decoupling, error handling, synchronization, serialization). It proposes a typed LocalStorageHandler utility class and a useDarkMode composable as solutions. A reader comment notes the author uses Pinia on Vue 3 instead.
one_line: Tutorial on using LocalStorage in Vue for persisting dark mode and other user settings, with typed utility and composable patterns.
key_facts: LocalStorage is a web storage API that stores data in the browser indefinitely and the data remains across browser sessions.
LocalStorage uses a key-value store model where both the key and the value are strings.
The LocalStorage methods covered are setItem, getItem, removeItem and clear.
The example dark mode component stores the preference under the key 'darkMode' using JSON.stringify.
The example component applies CSS custom properties --background-color and --text-color to document.documentElement.
The article lists five challenges: type safety and key validation, decoupling from LocalStorage, error handling, synchronization across components, and serialization constraints.
The article suggests a types file defining LocalStorageValues with darkMode as boolean, userSettings as UserSettings, and lastLogin as Date.
The LocalStorageHandler utility class exposes static getItem, setItem, removeItem and clear methods wrapped in try/catch blocks.
The useDarkMode composable creates a ref from LocalStorageHandler.getItem('darkMode') and uses a watch to call setItem when the value changes.
The article was posted on Apr 21 by Alexander Opalic and tagged webdev, vue, beginners and tutorial.
A top comment by richardev says 'Nice article. I use Pinia on Vue 3 tho'.'
